Divine speech introduces the scouting mi: One leader per tribe is sent, according to ancestral groups, into land explicitly given as a possession. Both commissioning and gift remain.
Moses sends them from Paran by the Lord's voice; all are identified as leaders.
Reuben's scout is Salamiel son of Zaccur in the selected Greek; the name is not replaced by the familiar Shammua.
Simeon's scout is Shaphat son of Souri. The inherited equivalents remain provisional and are recorded with Greek forms.
Judah's scout is Caleb son of Jephunneh, with both names retained.
Issachar's scout is Igal son of Joseph. Joseph here is the father, not the following tribal designation.
Ephraim's scout is Hoshea son of Nun, preceding the explicit renaming in verse 16.
Benjamin's scout is Palti son of Raphu; the father's form remains distinct from other conventional spellings.
Zebulun's scout is the selected Goudiel, represented provisionally as Gaddiel, son of Sodi.
Joseph and the sons of Manasseh both qualify this entry; the scout is Gaddi son of Susi.
Dan's scout is Ammiel son of Gemalli, with the selected name pair recorded.
Asher's scout is Sethur son of Michael.
Naphtali's scout is Nahbi son of Iabi; the inherited name pair is retained provisionally.
Gad's selected scout name repeats Goudiel, provisionally Gaddiel, with father Machi. It is not normalized to a different name to remove the repetition.
The list closes and Moses names Hoshea Joshua. Both conventional English forms preserve the explicit distinction between the two selected Greek names.
Moses sends them through this wilderness into the hill country. A southward instruction from another textual tradition is not inserted.
Land and inhabitants are inspected, with stronger/weak and few/many alternatives retained.
The land's quality and towns' walls are separate questions. The selected walled/unwalled contrast remains in that order.
Rich or neglected, presence of trees, perseverance and taking fruit remain. The selected seasonal statement says spring before grapes, and is not harmonized to a different harvest date.
column3: The compact season phrase and harvest supplied with grapes merit further lexical review.

Divine speech introduces the scouting mi: The route retains Sin, Raab and Ephaath rather than replacing them with conventional alternatives without a name decision.
Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai are identified with Anak's families; Hebron precedes Egyptian Tanis by seven years. All names remain provisional equivalents.
The scouts inspect the ravine, cut one grape cluster on a branch and carry it with pomegranates and figs. The selected plural carrying apparatus is retained without adding two bearers.
Ravine of the Cluster translates the Greek name and its explanation from the cut cluster.
Return follows forty days of inspecting the land. The number is unchanged.
Moses, Aaron and the whole assembly receive the report at Paran/Kadesh and see the fruit. The repeated assembly reference remains.
The report affirms the milk-and-honey land and points to its fruit, addressing the sender in the singular.
Bold inhabitants, strong walls, very large cities and Anak's family are all separate obstacles named by the speakers.
The selected Hivites are included among four hill-country peoples. Amalek's south and Canaanites beside sea and Jordan remain.
Caleb quiets the people toward Moses and answers no, followed by emphatic ascent, inheritance and ability. No subject is reversed.
The other scouts refuse ascent and emphatically deny ability because the nation is much stronger. Both negatives remain.
Dismay represents the selected report's effect; devouring land and exceedingly tall inhabitants remain the scouts' claims.
column3: The best English expression for bringing out dismay needs lexical and spoken-stage review.

Divine speech introduces the scouting mi: Giants and grasshopper comparison remain; both appearances are before them in the selected Greek. No first occurrence is changed to our own eyes.
The whole congregation cries out and the people weep all night. Both whole expressions remain.
All Israel grumbles against Moses and Aaron, wishing death in Egypt or this wilderness. Both alternatives remain.
War death and plunder of wives and children motivate the expressed preference for Egypt. This is the people's accusation, not the narrator's verdict.
They propose appointing a leader and returning to Egypt, in that order.
Moses and Aaron fall face down before the entire assembly.
Joshua and Caleb, identified among the scouts, tear their garments; their fathers remain named.
The doubled exceedingly preserves the source's repeated emphasis on the land's goodness.
Divine choosing conditions entry and gift of the milk-and-honey land. Choosing is retained rather than an unverified alternate sense.
The proposal replaces initial Only with But to express the selected adversative without adding a restriction. Deserters, food, departed season and the repeated fear prohibition remain.
The assembly calls for stoning; the Lord's glory appears in cloud above the tent among all Israel. Cloud is explicit in the selected text.
Two how-long questions concern provocation and unbelief despite the signs among them.
Death and destruction precede the promise to make Moses and his father's house a greater, more numerous nation. The father's house is explicitly retained.
Moses addresses God with Thy and Thou, appealing to Egypt's hearing and the power that brought Israel out.
All inhabitants have heard of divine presence, eye-to-eye appearance, cloud above and cloud/fire pillars ahead. The divine-address forms remain distinct from the people.
Wiping out the people as one man introduces the nations' prospective speech. The inherited conditional English is retained provisionally for the connected future scenario.
The nations' anticipated explanation alleges divine inability and slaughter in the wilderness. It remains inside the reported claim.
Moses requests exalted divine strength according to God's prior word, introducing the quotation.
Patience, abundant mercy and truth remain, with three wrongdoing terms, emphatic non-cleansing of the guilty and third/fourth generations. The selected fuller list is not shortened.
The petition seeks forgiveness according to great mercy and cites graciousness from Egypt until now.
The Lord declares present graciousness according to Moses' word, with ordinary your addressing Moses.
Both I live and My name lives are retained, followed by glory filling all the earth.
Seeing glory and signs, testing for the tenth time and not hearing the voice describe those excluded in the next verse.
column3: The connective relationship to the oath and glory statement needs fuller discourse review; the inherited punctuation remains provisional.

Divine speech introduces the scouting mi: The selected longer clause promises land to children here with God who lack knowledge of good and evil, including every inexperienced young person. The provoking adults remain excluded.
Caleb's different spirit and following God explain his entry; his seed inherits the land. The cause and promise both remain.
Amalek and Canaanites occupy the valley; Israel is ordered tomorrow toward wilderness by the Red Sea route.
The renewed divine speech addresses both Moses and Aaron.
The elliptical how-long question remains followed by grumbling before God and against the human addressees.
column3: How long with this congregation is awkward; the omitted verbal predicate needs careful spoken-stage handling without an unsupported addition.

Divine speech introduces the scouting mi: The divine life oath confirms action matching the people's words spoken into His ears.
Falling bodies, the entire enrolment and the twenty-and-upward grumblers remain in the sentence. The age threshold is not generalized to all adults.
The oath construction conveys emphatic non-entry, with Caleb and Joshua as named exceptions. The stretched-out hand and settlement purpose remain.
The threatened children instead enter and inherit the rejected land. Both actions reverse the people's prediction.
The repeated falling-bodies sentence remains unabridged.
Sons live as herders for forty years and bear their parents' whoredom until the bodies are consumed. The severe metaphor is not softened away.
Forty days correspond to forty years, a day for a year. Bearing sins and learning divine furious anger follow the selected wording.
The Lord's declared action targets the congregation united against Him; consumption and death both occur in this wilderness.
The returning scouts grumble against the land before the assembly and bring evil words concerning it. The target remains the land.
Those who spoke evil against the land die in the plague before the Lord.
Joshua and Caleb survive from among the scouts. Their identities and contrast with the dead remain.
Moses speaks to all Israel, and the people mourn greatly.
Early ascent and the admission of sin accompany the announced attempt to reach the promised place. The action is not presented as obeying a new command.
Moses identifies transgression of the Lord's word and warns that it will not go well.
The prohibition to ascend is explained by divine absence and impending defeat before enemies.
Amalek and Canaanites are ahead; sword defeat follows disobedient turning away. The repeated divine absence remains.
The people force their ascent while ark and Moses remain in camp. Neither is made to accompany them.
The enemies descend, rout and cut them down as far as Erman; the selected final return-to-camp clause remains.
column3: The final plural subject needs discourse review before replacing they with an explicit group.
